subsystems.name: Opacity tables
subsystems.role: what starlight actually interacts with: millions of spectral lines smeared into usable absorption coefficients.
parts: line lists (experimental and computed, e.g. HITRAN, HITEMP, ExoMol)
collision-induced absorption for H2–H2 and H2–He
k-distribution tables across temperature and pressure grids

subsystems.name: Radiative transfer forward model
subsystems.role: given a guess atmosphere, predicts the spectrum.
parts: transmission geometry (the limb) and emission geometry
instrument broadening to the observed resolving power

subsystems.name: Atmosphere parameterisation
subsystems.role: turns an atmosphere into a handful of numbers the sampler can explore.
parts: temperature–pressure profile (isothermal, polynomial, or physically motivated)
cloud deck pressure, opacity and particle size

subsystems.name: Nuisance and systematics model
subsystems.role: stops instrument artefacts being mistaken for molecules.

subsystems.name: Sampler
subsystems.role: maps the posterior probability over all parameters.
parts: neural simulation-based inference for expensive models

subsystems.name: Post-processing and model selection
subsystems.role: decides whether a detection is real.

buildSteps.title: Assemble opacity data
buildSteps.detail: Collect experimental and quantum-computed line lists for water, methane, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, sodium, potassium and others, plus collision-induced absorption for the hydrogen-dominated background.

buildSteps.title: Build k-tables
buildSteps.detail: Sort lines into wavelength bins, compute absorption across a grid of temperatures and pressures, and store pre-tabulated coefficients so a forward model is a fast lookup rather than a line-by-line calculation.

buildSteps.title: Write the forward model
buildSteps.detail: Lay the atmosphere out in pressure layers, set abundances and cloud properties, solve radiative transfer, and integrate across the stellar disk to produce a transit depth or planet-to-star flux ratio versus wavelength.

buildSteps.title: Parameterise the unknowns
buildSteps.detail: Reduce the atmosphere to free parameters — abundances, a temperature profile, cloud properties — plus nuisance parameters for the instrument and star, with physically sensible prior ranges.

buildSteps.title: Build the likelihood
buildSteps.detail: Compare the modelled spectrum to binned, calibrated data using Gaussian errors plus a jitter term that absorbs underestimated noise.

buildSteps.title: Sample the posterior
buildSteps.detail: Run nested sampling or MCMC over the full parameter space, checking convergence of the evidence and of individual parameters.

buildSteps.title: Compare models
buildSteps.detail: Recompute the evidence for nested models with and without each molecule or cloud, and use Bayes factors to decide what the data actually support.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate false positives
buildSteps.detail: Inject synthetic planets with known atmospheres into the real noise and re-retrieve them, to measure how often the pipeline claims a detection that is not there.

buildSteps.title: Publish posteriors
buildSteps.detail: Report parameter distributions, abundance detections with uncertainties, upper limits for everything else, and the assumptions that could change them.

prerequisites.tech: Molecular line lists and opacity databases
prerequisites.why: without accurate absorption data, a retrieval fits the wrong molecules at the wrong abundances.
the forward model must be accurate enough that its errors are smaller than the measurement errors.
these produce the full posterior and the evidence needed for model comparison.

prerequisites.tech: Space telescopes with stable, wide-wavelength spectroscopy
prerequisites.why: retrievals depend on low, well-characterised noise across many wavelengths, as JWST provides.
amortises the cost of very slow forward models, but calibration on real noise is still being established.
retrieved abundances are only interpretable when chemistry and mixing are modelled alongside the retrieval.

pathway.milestone: routine retrieval of JWST transmission and emission spectra for gas giants and small planets
pathway.unlocks: molecular inventories, cloud characterisation and, for some planets, tentative biosignature-related claims that then get tested.

pathway.milestone: hierarchical population retrievals across hundreds of planets
pathway.unlocks: statements about what planetary systems are like as a class, not just one planet at a time.

pathway.milestone: retrievals of reflected-light spectra from coronagraphic imaging
pathway.unlocks: atmospheres of planets far enough from their star to be temperate, though with far less signal.

pathway.milestone: end-to-end inference linking spectra to chemistry, formation history and habitability
pathway.unlocks: a defensible answer to whether a detected gas is biology — or just geology and photochemistry.
